facts.label: Regras com can e can’t
facts.sub: Use Can I + verbo para pedir permissão: Can I park here? Use You can e You can’t para dizer regras. Depois de can, o verbo fica na forma base.

facts.label: Pedindo
facts.sub: Para pedir permissão, use Can I + verbo base: Can I park here? Não use to depois de can. A resposta curta é Yes, you can ou No, you can’t.

facts.label: Regras
facts.sub: Para dizer o que é permitido, use can: You can park here for two hours. Para dizer o que é proibido, use can’t: You can’t stay all day. Can não muda com he, she ou it.

pages.title: A busy street · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Monday morning on a busy street in Nashville. Cars stop and go all along the road. Noah stops his car near a small bank. He wants a place to park. Officer Cody walks over with a ticket book. He has some rules for Noah.
“Excuse me! You can’t park here.” says Cody. “Oh, sorry. Can I park on the other side?” says Noah. “Yes, you can. But look at the sign.” says Cody.
